Definition: from G948; a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry:--abomination.
BiblicalUsage: Bdelygma is an abomination, a detestation. It is the word for the abomination of desolation Daniel spoke of that Jesus says will stand in the holy place, for the things highly esteemed among men that are abomination in the sight of God, and for the abominable works that will never enter the holy city.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe abomination is the Bible's strongest word for what God hates, because it is not dislike but detestation. The abomination in the holy place is the end of the story for a people who turned from God, and I hold that the city where no abomination enters is the home God is preparing for those who have left their abominations behind.
